title: Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Operator
raw_text:
10-15W. MOS 15W—Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Operator, CMF 15 (Rescind
202610)
     a. Major duties. A Soldier in MOS 15W engages in operating and remotely piloting the TUAS.
Performs pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight checks and procedures. Conducts site selection,
emplacement, and deployment of the air vehicles and ground equipment of the TUAS. Participates in
launch/recovery ground crew operations. Performs aircraft commander (AC) duties to include planning,
analysis, and execution of reconnaissance and security missions in support of targeting and information
collection. Operates, troubleshoots, and performs limited unit-level maintenance on communication
equipment, power sources, and wheeled vehicles.
Duties for MOS 15W at each level of skill are:
       (1) MOSC 15W1O. Executes reconnaissance and security missions. Plans and analyzes flight
missions. Deploys and redeploys the TUAS ground and air system. Launches and recovers the air
vehicle, performs pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight checks and procedures. Performs operator
maintenance and crew procedures on TUAS air and ground equipment. Prepares forms and records
related to TUAS air and ground support equipment maintenance. Participates in the TUAS site setup and
breakdown. Assists in proper handling and storage of flammable and hazardous materials.
       (2) MOSC 15W2O. Supervises and provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel
performing duties described in paragraphs a.1 and a.2. Performs operational checks and scheduled
inspections. Supervises and assists site setup and breakdown. Participates in mission planning including
terrain, threat, and current situation analysis. Participates in and supervises operator maintenance and
crew procedures performed on TUAS air and ground equipment. Serves as primary trainer of readiness
level (RL) 1 operators as the AC. Monitors proper handling and storage of flammable and hazardous
materials.
       (3) MOSC 15W3O. Performs duties described in paragraph a.1 and a.2. Performs, supervises, and
provides technical guidance to subordinate personnel performing TUAS operations, maintenance, and
crew procedures. Performs site selection using maps, aerial photographs, terrain analysis, and
information reports. Supervises site setup and breakdown. Coordinates with adjacent, higher, and
supported units. Conducts pre-combat checks and inspections. Supervises the conduct of after-action
reviews (AAR).
       (4) MOSC 15W4O. Performs duties shown in preceding skill levels (SL) and provides guidance to
subordinate Soldiers. Supervise operations and activities of the platoon. Applies the military information
collection and targeting process, reconnaissance, and security planning to TUAS operations. Conducts
and assists the development of the unit training plan.
     b. Physical demands rating and qualifications for initial award or reclassification of MOS.
       (1) The Tactical Unmanned Aircraft System (TUAS) Operator must possess the following
qualifications: Waivers, and/or exceptions must be approved by Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft
Rucker, AL 36362-1100, (https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
       (a) A physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
       (b) A physical profile of 222221.
       (c) Normal color vision.
       (d) Qualifying scores.
               (1) A minimum score of 102 in aptitude area SC.
               (2) A Minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) -0120 cm, Seated Power Throw
(PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036 shuttles in
Physical Demands Category “Moderate” (Gold).
       (e) A U.S. Citizen.
       (f) A high school graduate or equivalent.
       (g) A security eligibility of SECRET is required prior to attendance/arrival for training, initial award of
the MOS and to maintain the MOS. An interim SECRET security access granted by CCF meets this
requirement.
           (h) Complete, pass and maintain the Army Class IV medical physical prior to requesting and/or
granting the MOS to the soldier and his attendance/arrival to training/school. Not required to complete or
pass the Type II decompression sickness/chamber training requirement.
           (i) Formal training (completion of MOS 15W under the auspices of The United States Army
Aviation Center of Excellence (AVCOE) is mandatory.
             (j) Reclassification: Must meet the above qualifications and all prerequisites IAW AR 614-200
“Reclassification of primary military occupational specialty and/or secondary military occupational
specialty” chapter and AR 40-501 “Medical Fitness Standards for Retention and Separation, including
Retirement” chapter. MOS 15W is closed to individuals in the grade SGT or above unless they have
previously held MOS 15W/C/35K/96U for a minimum of 12 months at skill level 1 or 2, 18 months at skill
level 3 or 24 months at skill level 4.
                1. Active Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
determination packet to Cdr, AVCOE, ATTN: ATZQ-CDF-P, Ft Rucker, AL 36362-1100,
(https://home.army.mil/rucker/about/AVCOE/opfd/enlisted).
                2. National Guard: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a waiver
packet through National Guard Bureau, ATTN: NGB-ARNG-AV, 111 South George Mason Drive,
Arlington, VA 22204-1382(http://www.rucker.army.mil/usaace/directorates/cdid/opfd/iw_enlisted.html).,
                3. Reserve Component: Soldiers that do not meet the above qualifications must submit a
waiver packet through Commander, Army Reserve Aviation Command (ARAC), ATTN: G3 (AFAK-OPT),
1160 Brandenburg Station Road, Ft Knox, KY 40121-4190, (usarmy.usarc.arac.list.g-37-
training@army.mil
         (2) MOS closed for reclassification to Soldiers who have been deemed permanently non-
deployable in accordance with AR 40-501, AR 220-1, AR 600-8-101, and AR 614-30. Soldiers must meet
the minimum criteria for retainability stated in AR 635-40, paragraph 3-5(a) and be fully deployable to all
locations and echelons.
     c. Additional skill identifiers. (Note: Refer to table 12-8 for (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with
all enlisted MOS)).
       (1) F8---Unmanned Aircraft Systems Master Gunner
       (2) G3—Air Cavalry Leaders Course
       (3) U7-- Unmanned Aerial System (UAS) Instructor Operator (I/O)
     d. Physical requirements and standards of grade. Physical requirements and SG relating to each skill
level are listed in the following tables:
        (1) Table 10-15W-1. Physical requirements.
        (2) Table 10-15W-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
       (3) Table 10-15W-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
